case_summary: The plugin's render callback drops audio while synchronously locking, fetching configuration over HTTP, allocating scratch storage, and writing telemetry.
answer: Keep the audio callback as a bounded real-time processor. Move HTTP/config parsing to a control thread, validate settings there, and publish a fixed-size immutable snapshot through a bounded, nonblocking latest-value handoff; the callback checks once and otherwise keeps its previous snapshot. Allocate scratch storage before rendering. Send telemetry through a preallocated bounded queue for a background consumer, with an explicit drop policy when full. This keeps the callback independent of network availability and avoids waiting, allocation, and synchronous I/O; coalescing is appropriate because intermediate parameter states need not be preserved. A lock-free handoff adds synchronization complexity, so keep it narrow and prove its ownership/lifetime rules rather than sharing mutable config or using callback-side reference counting. Verify with static/code-level checks that the callback path has no locks, allocation, network calls, or blocking I/O; stress parameter changes and offline/network stalls; then measure worst-case callback duration and xruns on the target plugin host at 128 frames/48 kHz under representative CPU load. Desktop functional tests alone cannot establish the approximately 2.67 ms deadline or host-specific behavior. Kafka and service separation add no justified boundary without independent-service requirements.
